abstract:
The CafeShop Ordering and Management System is developed to address common operational challenges faced by cafés, including inefficient order management, delayed communication between customers and staff, and limited access to real-time business data. Traditional café operations often rely on manual order taking and paper-based processes, which may lead to order inaccuracies, slower service, and difficulties in tracking sales and operational performance.

To solve these issues, the CafeShop system provides a digital platform that integrates customer ordering, payment processing, and administrative management into a single system. Customers can scan a QR code assigned to each table to access a digital menu through their mobile devices, browse available items, select menu variations such as sizes, and place orders directly through the system. Payments are supported through PromptPay QR code integration using the Omise payment gateway, enabling a secure and convenient cashless payment experience.

For café staff and administrators, the system provides a web-based dashboard that allows real-time monitoring and management of orders, menu items, tables, and invoices. The system utilizes WebSocket technology to deliver instant notifications when new orders are placed, allowing staff to process orders efficiently. Additionally, administrators can monitor sales data and manage operational activities through a centralized interface.

By integrating digital ordering, real-time communication, and administrative management tools, the CafeShop system improves operational efficiency, reduces manual workload, minimizes ordering errors, and enhances the overall customer service experience in café environments.

abstract:
This project presents the development of a web-based Cosmetics Business Management System designed to improve operational efficiency in sales management and administrative processes at NYK Cosmetics, a retail and wholesale cosmetics business. The system aims to reduce manual workload by providing a centralized platform that integrates sales order management, inventory tracking, customer loan monitoring, and administrative reporting.

The application enables salespersons to record customer orders digitally through a web-based system, allowing them to access the platform conveniently from tablets or web browsers. The system automatically updates inventory and transaction records in real time after each order submission. Administrators can review, adjust, and manage orders through a centralized web dashboard without relying on manual record books or scattered spreadsheets. In addition, the system includes customer loan management features that allow administrators to track outstanding balances, monitor payment histories, and maintain accurate financial records efficiently. The system also provides statistical dashboards that display sales performance by product, shop, and region, enabling better decision-making and business analysis. By implementing this system, NYK Cosmetics can reduce operational errors and improve overall business management efficiency.

The system is developed using modern web technologies including Next.js for the frontend, Nest.js for the backend, and PostgreSQL for the database, and deployed on cloud infrastructure to ensure accessibility and scalability. Overall, the proposed system establishes a centralized digital platform that enhances operational management and supports the future growth of NYK Cosmetics.

abstract:
Proper road bike fitting is essential for cycling safety, performance, and injury prevention; however, professional bike fitting systems often require specialized equipment and expert assessment, making them costly and inaccessible to many cyclists. This senior project, developed by the First Safe Point team, addresses this problem by investigating a low-cost, vision-based approach for road bike posture analysis using computer vision techniques. The proposed system utilizes MediaPipe Pose Estimation to detect cyclist body landmarks from recorded road cycling videos and computes key joint angles, including knee, hip, elbow, ankle, and back angles. These angles are evaluated against industry-standard road bike fitting ranges to provide visual posture feedback.

This report presents the initial development phase of the system, focusing on pose detection, joint angle computation, and real-time visualization, as well as the evaluation of cyclists' perceptions of the posture feedback generated by the system.
